newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares tread water on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares tread water on uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Monday in sluggish trading as traders were sidelined by continued uncertainty, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares ended down 0.26 percent, or 0.73 points, to 284.98 on low all-share turnover of 112 million shekels ($31.2 million) against 117 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.37 percent lower at 292.09.

"The market continues to be very quiet as investors await further developments. As long as the shekel remains volatile and the political situation is unclear the market will continue to remain static," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investement and Securities.

In the latest shock to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's embattled government, Foreign Minister David Levy said on Monday he would decide in the coming days whether to resign in protest at Netanyahu's way of running the government.

The government narrowly survived a parliamentary no-confidence vote last week in which one-sixth of the coalition partners failed to support the governmnet. The cabinet is in meantime squabbling over a ministerial shake-up, which is expected to include Ariel Sharon's appointment as finance minister.

The shekel plunged five percent last week after the cabinet announced a reform of the exchange rate regime and the Bank of Israel lowered the base rate by a steep 1.2 percentage points to 12.7 percent.
"Its not clear yet where the shekel is going. This might be the beginning of a new trend or a temporary devaluation," Hoffman said.

He added that the latest decline in share prices mjight still be defined as a technical correction. "Since the beginning of the year the market gained more than 40 percent and a consolidation is a healthy move," Hoffman said.
"The market is trying to rise but because of all the uncertainty it cannot move," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.
"Investors are sitting on the fence awaiting further developments," she said.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which fell 1.25 percent to 545 agorot on turnover of 8.6 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which lost 1.0 percent to 748 agorot on volume of 4.8 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which closed unchanged at 423 agorot on turnover of 4.5 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 ($ = 3.584 Israeli Shekels)
